summary: Materialize a NEW project from a contract map: create the directories, write the files (boilerplate or documented stubs with FILE/ROLE/DOES headers), and emit PROJECT_PLAN.md. Preview-first; one apply for the whole batch.

action.description: archetypes: list built-in starting maps. show_archetype: return one map to tailor. plan: validate a map + preview every dir/file (writes nothing). create: materialize (needs apply:true).

archetype.description: show_archetype action: which built-in map to return (python-cli | web-app | records-project).

map.description: the project-map contract: {name, plan?, archetype?, tree:[{dir}|{file, content|template, role, does, depends_on, wires_to, plan}]}. tree overlays the archetype if both given.

root.description: destination directory (relative, confined to the work target / toolkit). Default: <output_root>/scaffold/<name-slug>.

overwrite.description: create action: replace files that already exist. Without it, any collision refuses the whole batch.

apply.description: create for real. Without it (or action=plan) you get a no-write preview.

base.description: absolute root the project is created under

provenance.note: E1. Map-driven new-project materializer. Deliberately dumb (honors a contract, plans nothing); writes only the project tree, escape-proof via resolve_within_roots, preview-first + batch-consent. The planning/orchestration layer is a separate future tool.
